Hi 👋🏾 I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby's Co-Founder and CTO. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

 - Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

 - Built a set of flexible, composable components in our design system that allow other engineers to build beautiful, consistent setup wizards across our product easily.

 - Helped a Product Engineer improve the information hierarchy and scannability of their design for viewing a candidate’s assessments. Recruiters can quickly parse information and pick out anomalies.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

 - You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. You’ll get to test out ideas with our own recruiting team and hiring managers who use Ashby every day (like me), and often hear customer feedback as early as the day you release.

 - This role has always had the commitment of both Benji (CEO & Co-Founder) and me: I’ve held the role, steadfastly championed it since we started hiring in 2020, and haven’t diluted its responsibilities as we’ve grown (in fact, we’ve doubled down).

 - You get to shape the UI and UX of a powerful and complex product. Our users need software that helps them move quickly while adapting to their unique workflows and preferences. As a result, our UI isn’t a simple chatbox, but it can’t rely on a sea of knobs and dials either. It needs to feel approachable to someone using it for the first time while offering increasingly powerful ways to customize and automate their work.

 

WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

Design Engineers come in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. Here are some reasons you might not enjoy the role:

 - You only want to work on design systems. While improving our design system is one of many responsibilities, you won’t be able to work on it exclusively.

 - You like to do extensive research and user testing before implementation. The beauty of being part-Engineer is that you can build conviction by shipping to a subset of users (including our own team) and gathering feedback!

 - You want everything to be perfect before it gets into a user’s hands. One of the drivers of our success is that we ship fast. While we appreciate the strive for perfection, we also realize it doesn’t need to be achieved all at once; instead, we iterate over time, often letting user feedback and business needs drive prioritization.

 - You don’t have excellent taste and execution in visual design. Design Engineers set the bar for visual design in our app and continually improve it, pushing its boundaries with each new feature or redesign.

 - You need company-driven process and structure to get your projects across the finish line. Sprint planning and well-defined project management processes are things you need or look to others to lead. You’d rather focus on the design and technical details.

 - You only want to do exciting work. We’re building a team of kind, collaborative folks. Customer issues and investigations are distributed across the team, including our high-level ICs.

 

WHAT SENIORITY/LEVEL TO APPLY FOR

We’ve posted levels from Junior to Staff. The higher the level, the more experience and alignment with the role we expect when reviewing your application and while interviewing. Please apply to the one that sets the right expectations.

 - Junior Design Engineer - You should have no more than 2 years of industry experience as a designer or engineer. We want to see projects (personal or professional) with at least a couple of users that showcase great visual taste and burgeoning talent in both UI/UX and Engineering.

 - Design Engineer (This Posting) - This posting covers both Mid and Senior levels. You have 2+ years of continuous experience (e.g., internships don’t count) as an Engineer or a Designer. You have good proficiency in both Design and Engineering, with exceptional proficiency in the discipline you practice full-time. Regardless of which discipline you’re coming from, we expect experience designing products and shipping code to hundreds of users (even if through side projects).

 - Staff Design Engineer - We’re looking for folks who’ve practiced our flavor of Design Engineering professionally. It may not be through a formal title, but you’ve made major contributions to a design system and designed and implemented features for hundreds of users and iterated on them through user feedback.

Internally, we do not use these titles, but Engineers are leveled based on proficiency (which you can read about here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/leveling-and-compensation).

 

WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

As we’ve set the standard for excellence in TA software, HR teams have pulled us into solving their problems in areas like onboarding and performance management.

 

ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (my Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 

MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They took customer problems and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional product-development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But, consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, at Ashby, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 

COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/d4679311-9dba-4031-bf5e-19ce78597ab1/calendar.png]
 

We also meet in person at least twice a year, once as a department and once as a company. You also have a small budget to meet up with folks in your city/region.

 

INCREASE LEVERAGE, NOT TEAM SIZE

We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:

 - Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 15x a day. A debugger that works out of the box. Everyone on the team has contributed to our developer experience 💪🏾.

 - Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) that we constantly improve. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video below).

 - AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/engineering/ai-ashby-engineering-and-the-future.

Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:

 
[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/4ea5f68e-c33e-4ac9-831a-e732bee4a303/8d94727a-46d8-42a2-9627-ddcd7f822f95/arjun.png]
 

And a demo of one of these building blocks:

PUT EFFORT INTO DIVERSITY

Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. Having seen my mother and partner build their careers as minority women in non-diverse fields, I want to make sure Ashby creates opportunities for the next generation of engineers from underrepresented groups.

Today, 25% of engineers and 50% of our engineering leaders at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. We are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.

 

WORK-LIFE BALANCE: IT’S A MARATHON, NOT A SPRINT

The intensity of work at Ashby should feel like a marathon, not a sprint (nor speed-walking). We work with urgency and ambition to build excellent software, but we don’t need to prove out a new software category or product-market fit. That requires ingenuity and thoughtfulness, and that doesn’t happen with unrealistic deadlines or sleepless nights.

Our remote, low-meeting, high-ownership culture gives you a lot of flexibility in how you structure your days and weeks. In practice, that means you keep your own hours, but there will be moments of intensity, like launching your feature at our annual user conference. We offer unlimited PTO, and you actually get to use it. Some of our most exceptional engineers take almost 30 days of vacation per year.

This way of working allows many of us on the team to be active parents, including Benji and me. I block off 1.5 hours every morning to spend with my daughter and drop her off at school.  Mujda https://www.linkedin.com/in/mujdaalamzai/ (Product Engineer) puts it best in an article https://nextplayso.substack.com/p/should-you-join-ashby about us: “I can say that Ashby is a great place to be a mom… No one bats an eye if I have to take my kid to a doctor’s appointment or have to work weird hours because childcare fell through.”

 

INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together through pair programming, designing, writing design system specs collaboratively, and discussing decisions. There are no leetcode or whiteboard exercises.

Our interview process is three rounds:

 - Introduction call with me (30m, live). Be prepared to screen-share examples of your work.

 - A second round where we either do a technical screen (1h, live) or a design take-home (~3h async, 30m live)

 - Three interviews, a deep dive into a past design system or design project, a design system interview, and the interview we didn’t do in the second round: technical screen or design take-home. (3h, live)

Depending on our leadership team’s bandwidth, we may start with an additional 30m screen with a recruiter.

I will be your main point of contact and prep you for interviews. Each round will have written guidance so you know what to expect. You’ll meet 3-4 people in Design Engineering (with 5-15 minutes in each interview to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!

 

YOUR FIRST THREE MONTHS AT ASHBY

We want an exceptional onboarding experience for every new hire. At Ashby, your dev environment is set up with a single script, you push your first product change on day one, and you spend the rest of your time shipping product changes that give you a tour of our codebase and best practices. The product changes increase in scope and ambiguity from simple copy changes to the delivery of a prominent, impactful feature. Your manager will do a 30, 60, and 90-day review to give feedback and calibrate on how we work together.

It’s a team effort to get you successfully onboarded; you’ll have a peer paired with you to answer questions, pair program, and check in often to see if you need help. The rest of the team will run training sessions on our culture, product, engineering process, and technical architecture.

 

TECHNOLOGY STACK

Our tech stack is TypeScript (frontend & backend), React, GraphQL API, Node.js, Postgres, and Redis. Depending on the level you’re applying for and your past experience, we expect, at a minimum, good proficiency with TypeScript, React, and CSS. Proficiency with backend technologies is a plus, as it allows you to work without coordinating with Product Engineers.

 

BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

 - A minimum of 12 weeks of fully paid parental leave, covered by Ashby. For folks outside the US, it may be longer to be in line with regional requirements.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

An overview of this role 
 As a Staff Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team in the US: the person who decides what "proven" means before something ships, and who helps shape what the team builds next, not just how to build it. It's a from-scratch, generalist team with no dedicated product manager — that ownership starts on day one.
 Some examples of the problems this team takes on:
 Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.
 Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.
 What you'll do 
 Set the technical direction for the team's agentic systems, from how agents are orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.
 Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.
 Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.
 Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.
 Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.
 Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.
 Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.
 Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.
 Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
 What you'll bring 
 Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.
 Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.
 Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.
 Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.
 A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.
 Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.
 A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.
 About the team 
 Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.
 It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.
 Remote-Global 
 The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity . Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

Ton rôle est de trouver les directeurs d'usine, les superviseurs de maintenance et les responsables des opérations dans les entreprises industrielles qui ont un vrai problème que nous pouvons résoudre, et de les mettre en contact avec un représentant aux comptes avant que quelqu'un d'autre ne le fasse.

 - Effectuer entre 70 et 100 appels sortants par jour auprès de décideurs en maintenance et en opérations dans des entreprises industrielles à travers l'Amérique du Nord

 - Bâtir des séquences multicanaux par téléphone, courriel et LinkedIn qui génèrent des réponses en parlant de vrais problèmes opérationnels, pas de scripts génériques

 - Qualifier les prospects rapidement et réserver des entrevues pour les représentants aux comptes, en ciblant les entreprises où MaintainX peut avoir un impact mesurable

 - Maintenir ton pipeline à jour dans Salesforce et assurer le suivi de chaque fil ouvert sans qu'on ait besoin de te le rappeler

 - Collaborer avec les représentants aux comptes pour comprendre ce qui convertit et affiner ton ciblage et ton approche au fil du temps

À 6 mois, le succès ressemble à un taux d'atteinte des SQLs supérieur à 90% et une approche sortante répétable que tu peux défendre. À 12 mois, les meilleurs BDR de cette équipe sont sur la voie d'un poste de clôture.

Ton profil

 - Expérience dans un environnement à volume élevé et résistant au rejet: ventes, recrutement, hôtellerie, commerce de détail, ou tout autre rôle qui a forgé ta résilience et ta capacité à établir rapidement un lien de confiance

 - Une réelle envie de décrocher le téléphone: le volume d'appels sortants, c'est le travail

 - Communication écrite et verbale claire et soignée en français et en anglais

 - Sens du suivi démontré: tu es responsable de ton pipeline et de tes chiffres sans qu'on ait besoin de te le rappeler

 - Baccalauréat requis

Atouts: expérience avec Salesforce, Outreach, ZoomInfo ou Nooks; expérience préalable en ventes B2B ou SaaS

Le titulaire de ce poste est chargé de gérer et d'accompagner un portefeuille de clients situés principalement sur les marchés anglophones (États-Unis et Canada anglophone), ce qui nécessite une communication quotidienne, à l'oral comme à l'écrit, en anglais avec ces clients.

Ce que nous offrons

 - Base compétitive et rémunération variable non plafonnée : les commissions sont versées sur l'atteinte des SQLs et les revenus conclus, sans plafond sur l'un ou l'autre

 - Véritable trajectoire de carrière : les BDR qui atteignent leurs objectifs ont un chemin clair vers un poste de représentant aux comptes ou de gestionnaire de comptes. La plupart de nos représentants actuels ont été promus de l'interne, et ce parcours se réalise généralement entre un an et un an et demi

 - Couverture santé, dentaire et vision dès le premier jour

 - Programme REER

 - Allocation de 1 000 $ pour le bureau à domicile et budget annuel de 1 000 $ pour le développement professionnel
   
   

Le salaire de base ne représente qu'une partie de la rémunération globale offerte par Autodesk. Pour les postes situés au Canada, la rémunération cible totale (OTE) de départ devrait se situer entre 87 500 $ et 96 500 $. L'OTE comprend le salaire de base et la commission cible pour les postes de vente. Les offres sont établies en fonction de l'expérience et de l'emplacement géographique du candidat et peuvent dépasser cette fourchette. En plus du salaire de base, la rémunération peut comprendre des primes annuelles en argent, des commissions pour les postes de vente, des attributions d'actions et un régime d'avantages sociaux complet.

Notre façon de travailler

Nous sommes en présentiel à Montréal, quatre jours par semaine. Nous investissons sérieusement dans les personnes que nous embauchons: université pour les nouveaux employés, mentorat dédié et formation en ventes concrète dès le premier jour. Nous grandissons rapidement et nous cherchons des personnes qui veulent grandir avec nous. L'humilité et le travail sérieux comptent autant que l'atteinte des objectifs, et les résultats parlent d'eux-mêmes: la plupart de nos représentants aux comptes et gestionnaires de comptes ont commencé exactement là où tu commences.

Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.
 We’re remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career. 
 The Role 
 This role puts you at the center of the team that independently challenges the models Square Financial Services relies on, from the credit models that decide who gets a loan to the forecasting models that shape the bank's plans. You'll help work out how to validate modeling approaches that are new to banking, often before an industry playbook exists. And with broad access to AI tools that few banks offer, you'll help rethink how validation itself gets done, so our team can run a rigorous program efficiently. If you enjoy digging into data and code, forming your own view of how a model really behaves, and explaining that view clearly to developers, leaders and bank examiners, this is the place to be.
As a Senior Model Risk Analyst, you will lead independent validations of models used across Square Financial Services (SFS), Block's bank, which lends to small businesses through Square Loans and to consumers through Cash App Borrow, and offers FDIC-insured deposits. Every SFS model must be independently reviewed and approved before it goes into use, so your work directly affects whether the bank can launch new products, grow lending and meet regulatory expectations safely and on time. You will report to the Head of AI & Model Risk and join the AI & Model Risk team, part of the bank's independent risk function. No two validations are alike: you will decide which tests matter for each model's data, methodology and intended use, with minimal day-to-day oversight.

 Lead independent validations across the model lifecycle, scaling the depth of your work to each model's risk rating

 Evaluate conceptual soundness: methodology, data, assumptions, limitations and any management adjustments to model outputs
 Verify that models work as intended: reproduce developer code (typically Python), test input data for accuracy and completeness with SQL, confirm outputs, and review evidence of accurate implementation, data integrity controls and security
 Build independent benchmark or challenger models for high-risk models, and perform outcomes analysis such as backtesting and rank-ordering tests
 Independently review each model owner's proposed risk rating and recommend a final rating
 Assess ongoing monitoring plans and results, review vendor models and pre-approved model changes, and flag models that are deteriorating before they become a problem
 Write clear validation reports, rate findings by severity, agree on remediation with model owners and track it to closure
 Present your conclusions to model owners, senior management and the bank's risk committees, and support internal audits and FDIC examinations
 Help keep the model inventory and validation records accurate, and build AI-enabled tools that make the validation program faster and more scalable

 Hands-on experience developing or validating statistical and machine learning models, and in-depth knowledge of the quantitative methods used to test them

 - Regulatory & Statutory Mastery: Solid command of Canadian federal and provincial payroll legislation (BC, Ontario, Quebec), CRA remittances, ROEs, and year-end T4 reconciliations.

 - Analytical Precision & Audit Rigour: Exceptional attention to detail with a proactive instinct for auditing data, spotting anomalies before submission, and resolving root-cause discrepancies.

 Correct-by-construction design flow

 Build constraints, checks and verified building blocks into the flow so that design intent (matching, parasitics, EM and density) is enforced during design rather than discovered at signoff. 
 Identify bottlenecks in the current delivery flow and prioritize improvements by their impact on design cycle time and schedule. 
 Turn issues found in deliveries into systematic checks so they are caught automatically on future projects.

About the Role

We are seeking an exceptional Principal Product Manager to build the HTS API Marketplace — the commercial and developer-facing layer through which enterprise partners access Hopper's lodging and cars capabilities.

This is a true 0-to-1 role. You will be the person who defines what it is: how capabilities are packaged and priced, how partners discover and integrate them, and how the marketplace evolves as a platform business. The underlying technical capabilities — connectivity orchestration, pricing and sort, content mapping, the extranet — are owned by dedicated capability teams. Your job is to work closely with those PMs to understand, package, and commercially expose those capabilities as coherent, enterprise-grade API products.

We expect this PM to move fast and build scrappily. You should be comfortable using AI tools and vibe coding to prototype workflows, mock APIs, and test partner experiences before handing off to engineering. The best candidate will reach for a prototype before a PRD.

You will partner with Engineering, Data Science, Commercial, Finance, and Supply — and coordinate tightly with other PMs across the organization — to bring the marketplace from concept to a revenue-generating platform.

This is a fully remote role.

 - Define what the HTS API Marketplace is: how capabilities are structured, packaged, and priced across a portfolio spanning HTS Connect, Search Polygons, Autocomplete, Ranking, Content & Property Mapping, Room Mapping, Deduplication/Auction, Pricing, Extranet, Taxes, and Custom Deals Engine.

 - Coordinate with capability PMs — who own the underlying technical systems — to understand each capability's roadmap, constraints, and customization surface, and translate that into externally-consumable API products.

 - Own the commercial model for the marketplace: platform vs. variable fee decisions, take rate structure per capability, enterprise packaging, and the custom deals framework for large partners with differentiated customer segments.

 - Build the developer and partner experience from scratch: API specifications, partner onboarding flows, documentation standards, sandbox environments, and integration tooling that minimizes time-to-first-value.

 - Use AI tools and rapid prototyping to test ideas quickly — mock API responses, prototype partner portals, simulate pricing and ranking configurations — before committing engineering resources.

 - Establish the go-to-market motion for the marketplace: work with Commercial to identify the right partners for each capability, sequence launches, and define what a successful commercial rollout looks like.

 - Own the marketplace revenue P&L: model and track GBV, take rate, and per-capability unit economics in partnership with Finance.
   

AN IDEAL CANDIDATE HAS:

 - 7+ years of Product Management experience, with at least one 0-to-1 product you built from concept to commercial launch.

 - Demonstrated experience building developer-facing or B2B marketplace products, including ownership of API product design, developer experience, and commercial packaging for enterprise customers.

 - AI-native working style: you use LLMs and vibe coding as first-line tools for prototyping, not as novelties. You have built working demos, mockups, or proof-of-concepts using AI before handing work to engineering.

 - Strong understanding of marketplace economics: take rates, supply-side incentives, demand-side optimization, and the design of platform vs. variable commercial models.

 - Ability to coordinate effectively across multiple product teams — you can synthesize roadmaps, surface dependencies, and drive cross-team alignment without owning the underlying engineering.

 - Experience working with external enterprise partners: translating commercial needs into product requirements and managing partner expectations through multi-phase rollouts.

 - Strong fluency with SQL and large-scale transactional or operational datasets.

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to write crisp API and product documentation.

Bonus:

 - Experience in travel commerce (lodging, cars, flights) or adjacent industries such as fintech, ads, or marketplace infrastructure.

 - Background in connectivity, distribution, or supplier technology (GDS, channel managers, OTA APIs).

 - Prior experience in Engineering, Data Science, or a technical role.

 - Familiarity with auction or deduplication mechanics, dynamic pricing systems, or recommendation and ranking models.
   

PERKS & BENEFITS OF WORKING WITH US:

 - Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and upsides of pre-IPO equity packages.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Carrot Cash travel stipend.

 - Open communication with management and company leadership.

 - Small, dynamic teams = massive impact.

More about Hopper

At Hopper, we are on a mission to become the leading travel platform globally – powering Hopper’s mobile app, website and our B2B business, HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions). By leveraging massive amounts of data and advanced machine learning algorithms, Hopper combines its world-class travel agency offering with proprietary fintech products to bring transparency, flexibility and savings to travelers globally. We have developed several unique fintech solutions that address everything from pricing volatility to trip disruptions – helping people travel better and save more on their trips.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based and is not an employment relationship.
 What this opportunity involves 
 We're looking for contributors to share their own medical lab report. You add the original files, and details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, and contact details, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. You also check the redacted preview before you submit. The lab's name and address, the test names, and the results stay in the report. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. The files help improve AI systems that read and understand medical documents. In this project, contributors may:
 Add the PDF file of their own lab report, for example blood test results;
 Take an iPhone photo of each printed page of the report and a screenshot of each page on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac;
 Check the redacted preview of each page and submit it only if all details that identify them are covered;
 Add one report per task;
 Submit clear files where every page of the report is fully visible.
 If you have your own lab test results and are comfortable sharing them once your personal details are covered, apply to take part in this project.
 What we look for 
 This opportunity is a good fit for people who have their own lab test results and are open to a short-term, project-based collaboration. To take part, contributors will need:
 To be 18 to 65 years old and live in one of these countries: the UK, Canada, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Brazil, Spain, Türkiye, Norway, Indonesia, the UAE, or Israel (no VPN while using Mindrift);
 Their own medical lab report as a PDF file (1 to 10 pages): lab test results only, such as a blood count, blood chemistry, or a urine test;
 A report from a lab in the country where they live, preferably in the local language (reports in English, or in both languages, are also accepted);
 A printed copy of the report, an iPhone (any model) for the photos, and an iPhone, iPad, or Mac for the screenshots.
 This opportunity is not suitable for someone else’s lab report (for example, a family member’s), a translated or edited copy of a report, or other medical documents such as discharge summaries or surgery notes. 
 How it works  
 Apply → Get an email from Mindrift Team (check spam too) → Register on Mindrift → Verify your identity → Sign the project consent form → Add your report's PDF, photos, and screenshots and check the redacted preview → Get paid for each accepted report 
 Privacy
 Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part doesn’t affect your Mindrift account. Before your first task, you read and sign a project consent form. Details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as doctors' names and signatures, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. Your original files are deleted. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. We never ask you to send your report by email, chat or anywhere outside the Mindrift platform.
 Project time expectations 
 Each lab report is a separate task, and you can add reports whenever it suits you while the project is active. This is a time-limited project, and the number of reports we can accept is not guaranteed. Reports need to meet the listed criteria to be accepted. If a report needs a fix, it comes back to you with the reason. 
 Earnings  
 Paid per accepted report:  $10 for every lab report  (PDF, photos, and screenshots of each page) that passes our quality checks. Earnings are added to your Mindrift balance once the report is accepted. 
 You can withdraw them to your bank account or PayPal via Tipalti, or via Payoneer (minimum $20). Payouts are processed twice a month. Mindrift doesn't deduct any fees, but your payment provider may charge a small transfer fee.

Waabi’s Commercial Product team defines and delivers the end-to-end commercial product that makes autonomous trucking deployable, scalable, and valuable to customers. We sit between autonomy, operations, sales, and customers, turning driverless capability into a real-world product that can be launched, sold, operated, and scaled.
We are hiring a commercially minded, operationally pragmatic Senior Manager to define how driverless trucking works as a scalable commercial service.
You will own the design and evolution of Waabi’s driverless operating model across the full Life of a Load, with a particular focus on our Driver-as-a-Service model, where customers own and operate their trucks while Waabi provides the autonomous Driver and supporting services.
This is a role for someone who enjoys broad ownership, navigating complex operational challenges, and getting into the details of how things actually work. You’ll help answer some of the most important questions in commercializing driverless trucking: How should the service work? What should Waabi own versus the customer? What happens when things don’t go according to plan? And how do we build a model that delivers a reliable customer experience while scaling economically?
A central part of the role is Mission Control, Waabi’s 24/7 control room that oversees driverless activity on the road. Mission Control monitors operating conditions, including weather, traffic, and road conditions, and provides remote assistance to Waabi Driver trucks in the field.
While Operations owns the day-to-day execution of Mission Control, you will own the commercial product requirements and capabilities that enable it to support safe, reliable, and scalable driverless operations. You will help shape its long-term operating architecture, including the capabilities, capacity, and systems needed as the fleet grows.
You will also define the requirements for off-nominal response: how the system, people, and supporting services work together when a load deviates from its planned execution. This includes everything from remote assistance and roadside service to vehicle recovery and first-responder interactions.
Your work will help establish the foundation for how driverless trucking operates commercially, not just for our first deployments, but for thousands of trucks operating across a national network.
What You’ll Own
You’ll own the commercial operating model and help drive the decisions that turn autonomous driving capability into a reliable, scalable transportation service.
Life of a Load: Define the end-to-end operating model, from a customer’s load order through delivery. Establish the workflows, handoffs, responsibilities, and supporting services required across Waabi, customers, and ecosystem partners. Determine what Waabi should provide, what customers should own, and how those responsibilities evolve as the service scales.
Mission Control: Define the commercial requirements and roadmap for Mission Control, including operational domain monitoring, remote assistance, exception handling, and customer communications. Work with software product, operations, and technical teams to determine which capabilities are needed for initial deployments and how they should evolve to support a growing fleet.
Off-Nominal Operations: Define how the service responds when a load deviates from its plan, including vehicle breakdowns, road closures, unexpected operating conditions, and other disruptions. Establish the service requirements, responsibility boundaries, and escalation models, working with Operations, Systems, and Safety to develop executable response protocols.
Roadside Services and Recovery: Define the third-party services and capabilities needed to support driverless trucks on the road, including roadside assistance, towing, recovery, and first-responder coordination. Determine appropriate service coverage, response expectations, partner responsibilities, and the tradeoffs between service quality, cost, and scalability.
Customer Service Experience: Define what customers see, do, and expect throughout the Life of a Load. Establish service visibility, communication, support, and resolution requirements. Partner with Account Management to define service commitments that are commercially compelling and operationally achievable.
Commercial Scalability: Turn early deployment solutions into repeatable, scalable capabilities. Make practical tradeoffs between customer experience, reliability, operational complexity, and cost. Help establish an operating model that can expand across customers, corridors, and fleet sizes without requiring a proportional increase in human support.
What Success Looks Like
Success means Waabi’s driverless service works as a product: it scales, it holds up commercially, and customers trust it.
You will have:
Established a clear Life of a Load operating model for Driver-as-a-Service, aligned across Operations, Safety, Autonomy, Engineering, and Account Management, with defined responsibilities, service requirements, costs, and outstanding decisions.
Enabled driverless launch readiness by defining the commercial requirements for off-nominal response, roadside services, recovery, and customer support, and working with Operations and Safety to ensure the necessary capabilities and protocols are in place.
Built a Mission Control product roadmap that identifies the capabilities required for launch and scale, with clear priorities for Engineering and a path toward improving operational efficiency as the fleet grows.
Created a clear and reliable customer service experience, where customers understand what Waabi provides, what they are responsible for, and how issues are communicated and resolved.
Established a scalable commercial service model, with visibility into support costs, operational dependencies, and the capabilities needed to improve unit economics as deployments expand.
Who Does Well at Waabi
There is no single path to this role, and many strong candidates will not come from autonomous trucking. We’re particularly interested in people who have built, launched, or scaled complex services where technology and physical operations come together.
Relevant backgrounds include:
Commercialization and Business Operations: You’ve helped bring a new technology or service to market, designing the operating model, customer experience, and supporting capabilities needed to make it commercially viable.
Transportation and Logistics: You’ve designed or transformed how transportation services operate, with firsthand experience in dispatch, service delivery, exception management, and operational economics.
Fleet Technology and Services: You’ve introduced new technologies into complex fleet operations, connecting vehicles, technology providers, customers, and service partners.
Autonomous Systems and Robotics: You’ve helped design or commercialize autonomous services, including the human support, remote operations, and exception management required to operate reliably.
Whatever your background, you’ve built or materially redesigned an operation rather than only run one. You bring strong commercial judgment, enjoy solving messy real-world problems, and care as much about whether a solution makes economic sense as whether it works.
Qualifications
8+ years of experience in commercial product management, business operations, commercialization, or related roles, with meaningful experience in technology-enabled physical-world businesses such as transportation, logistics, fleet services, robotics, industrial operations, or field services.
Demonstrated experience designing, launching, or scaling complex operational services that bring together technology, physical assets, people, customers, and external partners.
Strong commercial judgment and a practical approach to problem-solving. You understand how to balance customer needs, operational feasibility, cost, and scalability.
Demonstrated ability to take ambiguous, cross-functional problems, establish a clear direction, make decisions, and drive solutions through implementation.
Ability to work effectively across Product, Engineering, Operations, and commercial teams, influencing decisions without direct authority.
Comfortable working at both strategic and tactical levels, from defining a long-term operating model to working through the details of an individual customer workflow or operational exception.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex problems, articulate tradeoffs, and drive alignment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience taking a new technology-enabled product or service from initial concept or pilot through commercial launch and scale, ideally in an early-stage or rapidly growing company.
Experience designing and scaling customer-facing services, including service-level commitments, support models, operational responsibilities, and exception management.
Experience in transportation, logistics, fleet operations, or other businesses involving complex physical operations and distributed assets.
Experience developing and managing third-party service ecosystems, including partner selection, contracting, service requirements, and performance management.
Experience working with Product and Engineering teams to translate operational needs into technical capabilities and influence product roadmaps.
Familiarity with autonomous systems, remote assistance, fleet response, safety-critical operations, or other human-in-the-loop operational environments.

About Us: 
 At Reusables, we’re driven by a vision of a waste-free world and recognize the urgent need to address the environmental impact of our current systems and habits. We believe that meaningful change requires institutions to offer frictionless systems that make sustainability effortless and tangible. 
 What began as a grassroots initiative offering reusable takeout containers to restaurants and cafes in Vancouver, has since grown into an enterprise technology platform reaching institutions across North America. Today, Reusables is helping to eliminate thousands of tonnes of single-use waste each year, empowering businesses to join the journey toward a cleaner, more sustainable future. 
 As a venture-backed and mission-driven company, we are passionate about making impact at scale. We are a young, weirdly talented group of ‘high-octane’ individuals that are relentlessly focused on the planet, people, and profit – in that order. 
 About the Role: 
 You’ll build our products, and keep the ones already in the field working. Every Smart Return Bin, Smart Return Station and Smart Media unit we ship passes through your hands, and you’ll get to see your builds in use on campuses across North America every day. 
 You’ll start in January and learn the builds from our existing assembly team. You’ll work from written instructions, and you’ll have a real say in making those instructions, and our products, easier to build. 
 Our hardware is designed, built, tested and shipped by a small team in Vancouver, and you’ll report to our Hardware Lead. Most units ship in a summer peak, ahead of each autumn semester. 
 We’re moving from build-to-order to levelled production. From February we build steadily towards the September peak, and servicing and refurbishing units already in the field runs alongside new builds. 
 This is a full-time, permanent position, starting in January 2027. 
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Assemble Smart Return Bins, Smart Return Stations, Smart Media units and their subassemblies from work instructions, drawings, wiring diagrams and BOMs 
 Hit weekly build targets through the February build-ahead and the summer peak, so units are ready before customers need them 
 Check your own builds before they go to test, and flag repeat defects to our SI&T engineer and Hardware Lead 
 Repair, rebuild and retest units returned from the field, working from our SI&T engineer’s diagnosis. Servicing is year-round work, and part of how we keep reliability high 
 If a step is unclear or wrong, raise it and help fix the work instruction so the next build is easier 
 Bring “this part is hard to fit” and “this step takes forever” problems to engineering 
 Keep your bench ESD-safe, tidy and organised 
 Help with kitting, packing and shipping during the peak 
 How Your Year Looks: 
 January: Onboarding and training on every product, working towards building each one without supervision 
 February to May: Steady subassembly and unit builds ahead of the summer, refurbishment, prototype builds and help setting up fixtures 
 June to September: Final assembly, quality checks and packing during the peak 
 October to December: Refurbishment and returns, Smart Media builds, and a post-season review of what slowed the line 
 Where Your Role Ends: 
 You’ll work closely with the rest of the hardware team. These sit with them: 
 Setting the production schedule and daily priorities 
 Ordering parts, freight and customs 
 Test development and fault diagnosis 
 Owning the work instructions (you’ll feed in fixes) 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team: 
 Hands-on electromechanical or electronics assembly experience 
 You can read assembly drawings, wiring diagrams and BOMs 
 Soldering and hand-tool skills 
 You follow written instructions closely and care about getting it right 
 Eligible to work in Canada, and able to work full-time on-site in Vancouver 
 Available to start in January 2027 
 A positive, go-getter attitude: you’re excited by a new challenge every day, and you’ll figure out what you don’t know yet 
 Self-motivated and high ownership: give you a problem and you’ll own it through to the end, without waiting to be told how 
 No ego: we’re focused on the mission and check our egos at the door 
 Nice to have 
 IPC-A-610 or J-STD-001 certification 
 ESD-safe working practice 
 Repair or refurbishment experience 
 Startup or small-team experience 
 If your background doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications listed, but you’re confident in your ability to excel in this role, we still want to hear from you! At Reusables, we value diverse experiences and unique perspectives, so don’t hesitate to apply if you believe you can make a meaningful impact. We hire for attitude first. Skills can be taught, so we’d rather meet someone who takes on any task with excitement and figures it out, than someone held back by what they’ve done before. 
 We sincerely appreciate the time and effort of all applicants who express interest in joining our team. While we carefully review each application, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you for considering Reusables as your next career opportunity! 
 Compensation & Key Details
 Please note : This is an in-office position at our office in Vancouver, BC. 
 Compensation: $55,000–$65,000 CAD per year 
 Start date: January 2027 
 Reports to: Hardware Lead 
 Why You’ll Love Working At Reusables: 
 Benefits package (dental, vision, health) 
 Membership to Outdoor Prolink for discounted outdoor gear 
 A small, fun, low-ego team that loves the work we do together and the impact we have 
 A central, spacious and easy-access office in Vancouver with a friendly, sociable atmosphere and plenty of space to focus 
 Annual offsite with the entire Reusables team 
 Work that ships: what you build, buy or plan ends up on campuses where people use it every day 
 Our Values: 
 Strive for excellence 
 Assume you have something to learn from everyone 
 Play bigger 
 Check your ego at the door 
 See the path forward, not the trees in the way 
 Why Join Us: 
 The ocean already contains 165 million tonnes of plastic, and by 2050, plastic waste could outweigh fish. While recycling is often touted as the solution, only 5% of plastic is actually recycled in the U.S. (9% in Canada). Governments and businesses worldwide are banning single-use plastics and committing to zero-waste solutions by 2030. 
 Reusable packaging is the most sustainable alternative, but adoption has been hindered by cost and operational complexity. Reusables removes these barriers, offering a scalable, tech-enabled solution for food businesses and the institutions that serve them.

We strongly encourage applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, ancestry, place of origin, national origin, Indigenous identity, religion, political belief, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family status, physical or mental disability, or a criminal conviction unrelated to the role.

 Our Engineering organization owns the software that makes our marketplace work. The Data Platform group supports everyone at Faire who depends on data: Product Engineering, Data Science, Machine Learning, Analytics, Strategy, Finance, and Product. Our job is to make sure the data is there, it's right, and people can find it and query it without having to think about the plumbing underneath.

POSITION SUMMARY:

We're hiring a Senior Business Development Manager to identify, sign, and launch new reselling partners for Trulioo. This is a hunter role: you own the full cycle of, sourcing, qualifying and building prospective partners, negotiating and closing partnership agreements, and driving each new partner through onboarding to their first revenue.

Where our Partner Success team grows and retains existing partners, you focus on net-new: finding the platforms and companies whose customers need identity verification, convincing them that Trulioo is the best solution to embed and resell, and getting them live and producing. Your remit will be global — while you're based in North America, you identify and pursue partner opportunities across multiple markets worldwide, following where industry trends and demand for identity verification are creating new opportunities. You carry a partner-acquisition target and are measured on the number and quality of partners you sign and successfully launch. Signing a partner is the beginning of the relationship. You partner closely with the Partner Success team staying engaged well beyond launch to jointly drive the partnership's early momentum and long-term success. You'll work across Business Development leadership, Partner Success, Legal, Product, Technical Account Management, and Marketing to move partners from first conversation to a thriving, growing relationship.

This will be a full-time, permanent position working remotely out of North America, with a preference for USA-based applicants.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

 - Identify opportunities across markets and industry trends. Track industry trends, regulatory shifts, and emerging demand for identity verification across global markets to identify where new partner opportunities are opening — and prioritize the markets and verticals with the strongest potential.

 - Build and own a global pipeline of prospective partners. Research markets worldwide and identify identity orchestration, risk decisioning, onboarding, and other platforms whose customers need identity verification and who are a strong fit to resell Trulioo.

 - Prospect and open new relationships. Run outbound outreach and leverage your network and industry presence to initiate conversations with target partners.

 - Qualify and prioritize partner fit. Evaluate prospective partners on commercial potential, technical fit, market reach, and strategic value; focus effort on the partnerships most likely to drive meaningful revenue.

 - Make the case for Trulioo. Deliver compelling pitches and product positioning to partner executives and commercial teams, articulating the value of embedding and reselling Trulioo's KYC, KYB, and AML solutions.

 - Negotiate and close partnership agreements. Lead commercial negotiations and work with Legal and compliance to structure, negotiate, and close reseller agreements.

 - Launch new partners to first revenue. Drive onboarding and go-to-market launch for each new partner — coordinating enablement, technical integration, and launch marketing — with a focus on speed to first deal.

 - Coordinate technical onboarding. Partner with Technical Account Management and Product to scope and stand up each new partner's integration so they can go live as quickly as possible.

 - Drive launch GTM with Marketing. Work with Marketing on partner launch and co-marketing activities that generate early pipeline for the new partnership.

 - Partner with Partner Success throughout the relationship. Work hand in hand with the Partner Success team from signing onward — jointly building the account plan, aligning on launch and growth strategy, and staying engaged beyond launch to help the partnership reach its full potential.

 - Maintain forecast and reporting discipline. Keep an accurate pipeline of prospective partners in our CRM; report regularly on sourcing, signings, launches, and attainment against your acquisition target.

 - Be the voice of the market internally. Feed partner and market intelligence back to Product, GTM, and BD leadership to sharpen partner strategy, targeting, and positioning.

 - Leverage AI-driven market insights. Use AI-assisted research to identify emerging partner ecosystems, regulatory trends, and whitespace opportunities that drive our global partner acquisition strategy.

 - Champion AI-enabled ways of working. Experiment with and continue to deploy best practices for using AI to improve business development workflows, account planning, content creation, and knowledge sharing across the team. 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 10+ years in channel/partner sales, business development, or alliances, ideally within fintech, SaaS, or identity/fraud/compliance solutions.

 - A demonstrated track record of sourcing, signing, and launching new partners — and of carrying and hitting partner-acquisition or partner-sourced revenue targets.

 - Experience identifying and developing partner or business opportunities across multiple international markets, and comfort reading industry trends to prioritize where to play.

 - Strong full-cycle sales skills: prospecting, qualification, executive-level pitching, and closing.

 - Experience negotiating and structuring commercial partnership or reseller agreements, and working with Legal to close them.

 - Comfort with technical, API-driven products and coordinating technical onboarding to get partners live.

 -  Excellent communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

 -  Proficiency with CRM and partner management tools (e.g., Salesforce, PRM platforms).

 -  Comfort operating independently in a remote, fast-moving environment, working across global time zones and markets from a North American base.

 - Extensive experience using AI-powered productivity and sales tools to improve research, prospecting, pipeline management, and customer engagement.

 - Experience incorporating AI into day-to-day workflows while maintaining critical thinking, sound judgment, and a customer-first approach.

NICE TO HAVE:

 - Direct experience with identity verification, fraud prevention, KYC/KYB/AML, or regulatory compliance solutions.

 - Familiarity with identity orchestration, risk decisioning, or onboarding platforms and how they resell or embed third-party verification solutions.

 - An established network across fintech, banking, or digital commerce that can be activated to source partners.

 - Experience standing up or scaling a partner/channel program from early stages.

 - A track record of collaborating closely with post-sales or account management teams to grow partnerships over time.

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

WHY JOIN US:

At Trulioo, our partners help extend digital trust to more people and businesses around the world — and this role builds that network from the ground up. You'll scan global markets for the platforms that will carry Trulioo into new regions and verticals, close the partnerships that expand our reach, and stay with them as they grow. 

Thriving at Trulioo
